definitions.gloss: to spare, to devote, to set aside
definitions.explanation: To allocate or devote time, effort, resources, or space for a particular purpose. Often implies carving out something from a limited supply.
To tear or split something apart by pulling. A physical sense that is less common in modern everyday usage but appears in literary contexts.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}を{割|さ}いてくれた。
{研究|けんきゅう}に{多|おお}くの{予算|よさん}を{割|さ}いた。
examples.english: We devoted a large portion of the budget to research.

examples.japanese: お{忙|いそが}しいところ{時間|じかん}を{割|さ}いていただきありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for taking time out of your busy schedule.
I tore the cloth apart by hand.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{仲|なか}を{割|さ}くことはできない。
examples.english: You cannot tear those two apart.

examples.japanese: {群衆|ぐんしゅう}を{割|さ}いて{前|まえ}に{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: I pushed through the crowd and moved forward.

notes:
Godan verb (く row: {割|さ}く → {割|さ}かない → {割|さ}いて). Not to be confused with the homophone {裂|さ}く, which focuses on tearing/splitting and is written with a different kanji.

Sense 1 is much more common in modern usage. The pattern ～を{割|さ}く is typically used with {時間|じかん}, {人手|ひとで}, {予算|よさん}, or {紙面|しめん} (page space).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{時間|じかん}を{割|さ}く — to spare time
・{人手|ひとで}を{割|さ}く — to allocate personnel
・ページを{割|さ}く — to devote pages/space to
・{労力|ろうりょく}を{割|さ}く — to devote effort
